chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gifts a female slave on the condition that he is rewarded (with sexual access), but he is not rewarded; is it for him to take her back? He said, 'Yes, if he had stipulated it for him.' I said, 'Do you see if he gifted it to him and did not reward him, does he have sexual access to her or not?' He said, 'Yes, if he had not stipulated it for him when he gifted it.'

key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: he has sexual access to her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reclaiming a gifted female slave if the condition of sexual access is not met?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the revocability of a gift (hiba) of a female slave based on the explicit stipulation of sexual access (ithab), distinguishing between conditional gifts where reclamation is permitted upon breach, and unconditional gifts where the donor retains access rights. This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic view that 'ithab' can function as a conditional clause (shart) rather than merely a description of the gift's nature, ensuring the donor's intent is legally respected. The hadith underscores the importance of precise contractual stipulations in personal status law within the Shia tradition.
